title: POC scoping - benchmark harness integration
summary: Initial POC scoping focused on integrating DataHarbor's load scripts with Redwood's benchmark harness. Discussed workload sizing (concurrent sessions, token distribution), streaming vs non-streaming behavior, success criteria (latency p99, throughput, cost per 1M tokens), security constraints (VPC, KMS), and timelines for a two-week benchmark followed by a pilot. Agreed to share harness repo, sample configurations, and run an initial smoke test next week.
action_items: Priya Nair: share benchmark harness GitHub link and example config by 2026-11-11
Evan Cole: provide customer load scripts and token distribution CSV by 2026-11-12
Tom Becker: confirm networking/access constraints and firewall rules by 2026-11-13
next_steps: Redwood to fork customer's load scripts into harness and run smoke test (estimated 2 days)
Schedule 1-hour benchmark kick-off session w/ both infra teams (proposed 2026-11-16)
Share security checklist and required access docs (Redwood)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (DataHarbor HoML), Rina (Platform), Tom (SRE)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to focus today on the benchmark plan and hooking up your existing load scripts into the redwood harness, um quick intro from our side, priya's our lead SE on benchmarks
[00:18] Evan: yep thanks Jordan, Evan here, we built a set of load tests that mimic our real traffic, mainly streaming chat sessions and some batch non-streaming requests for embeddings, we want the POC to answer latency p99 and cost curves across 3 model variants
[00:35] Priya: great, that aligns, quick question - are the scripts you'll provide stateful chat sessions or stateless single-request flows? that impacts KV cache behavior and session routing
[00:50] Rina: mostly stateful - each session is a user conversation average 8-12 turns, token length varies, we can export a token distribution CSV. we also have a separate batch job that calls embeddings in bulk (about 10k docs)
[01:10] Tom: and from infra side, we are strict on network egress, we'll likely run the harness from within our VPC or on-prem - need to confirm firewall rules; KMS is in use for keys
[01:25] Jordan: noted, we'll include VPC deployment notes - Priya will follow up on KMS/HSM integration checklist. for the harness, typical flow is we ingest your scripts, map them to our scenario runner, and then run load tests both streaming and non-streaming to measure p50/p95/p99 and token/sec throughput
[01:48] Evan: can you run streaming and non-streaming using the same harness or are there differences?
[01:54] Priya: same harness, different runners - streaming opens a persistent connection and emits tokens as they're generated; non-streaming waits for full-response. streaming metrics are trickier because tail latency and connection churn matter, so we instrument per-chunk latencies; also KV cache hit rates change behavior
[02:20] Rina: we saw discrepancies in other vendors where streaming seemed faster for small messages but cost more because of more tokens and re-sends - we want to quantify that tradeoff
[02:35] Priya: absolutely, we'll include cost-per-conversation and cost-per-1000 messages in the report. we'll also estimate cost for our recommended batching/caching settings.
[02:48] Tom: on sizing - what concurrency should we test to mimic our 95th percentile? we currently see about 1.2k active concurrent chats during peak across region A
[02:59] Evan: yes 1.2k peak, average session length about 3 minutes, about 20 tokens/sec on average per session at peak due to multi-turn typing
[03:12] Priya: ok that's helpful - for the POC baseline we'll propose three phases: smoke (10-20 concurrent), ramp (up to 500), peak (1.2k). we'll capture token/sec, p99 generation latency, CPU/GPU utilization on the Redwood side, and observe fallback behavior if capacity is constrained
[03:34] Jordan: and success criteria? Evan, what would make this a success from DataHarbor's perspective?
[03:40] Evan: hard SLOs - p99 generation latency under 700ms for short-turn messages (<128 tokens), throughput to support 1.2k concurrent at our avg token/sec without errors, and cost below our current baseline by at least 15% for the common workload. also security - we need audit logs and retention controls
[04:02] Priya: we'll target those and instrument audit log sampling. Redwood has a dedicated mode if you want committed capacity, but for the POC we'll run on a sandboxed dedicated-like pool in hosted to simulate reserved throughput
[04:18] Rina: on the security note, do you have SOC 2 and SAML SSO compatibility? we'll need the security docs to review with compliance
[04:27] Jordan: yes SOC 2 Type II - we'll share the security packet. SAML SSO is standard for the console, and we support KMS for key management.
[04:36] Tom: returning to harness integration - our scripts are node-based and use a custom websocket wrapper for streaming, will that map into your runner?
[04:46] Priya: we have connectors for websockets and for HTTP streaming. sometimes the websocket implementation varies; if you can provide a small sample (10 sessions) we can validate parsing and chunk boundaries. sometimes transcripts show mis-splits - you might see 'K-V cash' in transcripts instead of 'KV cache' in automated outputs, small transcription noise, but the harness metrics are clean
[05:12] Evan: cool, we'll drop a small bundle this afternoon to the shared s3 link.
[05:18] Jordan: perfect. timeline wise, we propose: day 0-2 repo intake and smoke runs, day 3-6 full ramp and peak runs, day 7 analysis and a results review call. we'd expect the POC benchmark phase to be about one week, then if everything looks good a 2-3 week pilot for production validation
[05:40] Rina: what's required for us to run the harness inside our VPC?
[05:44] Priya: we'll provide an AMI/container image and a terraform module that deploys an ingress proxy with certs; you just need to open outbound to redwood-managed endpoints or we can run fully on-prem with a private package. we'll also need an IAM role for S3 access to pull scripts
[06:08] Tom: firewall team will need IP ranges and a temp test account; can you give a short checklist?
[06:12] Jordan: yes we'll attach a network checklist - Priya will also send required ports and sample security policy.
[06:20] Evan: about metrics - we'd like for the harness to output a CSV with per-run p50/p95/p99, tokens produced, cost estimate, and notes about streaming chunk sizes. can you include model variant labels so we can map results?
[06:34] Priya: yes, outputs include: run_id, model, streaming_flag, concurrency, p50/p95/p99, tokens_total, tokens_generated, cost_estimate_usd, kv_cache_hit_rate. we can also attach per-request traces for a subset for debugging
[06:51] Rina: do you support synthetic user delays to simulate thinking/typing? our traffic has inter-message think time distribution
[06:58] Priya: yes harness supports pause distributions; you can feed a distribution file. it also supports variable token payloads per turn.
[07:08] Tom: on fallback behavior - if capacity hits a ceiling do you auto-fallback to cheaper model variants? we need deterministic behavior, not opaque routing
[07:17] Jordan: by policy - we'll configure deterministic fallback rules for the POC: when latency > threshold OR queuing > X, route to a compatible smaller model and flag in metrics. we'll make fallbacks explicit in the reports
[07:31] Evan: competitors - we've tested with Anthropic and OpenAI, we'll include those baseline numbers. can Redwood run the same workloads so we have apples-to-apples?
[07:41] Priya: yes we'll parameterize the model and runtime to match tokenization and batching conditions to keep comparisons fair. note some differences in tokenizers can change token counts; we'll normalize by raw text inputs and report token deltas
[07:58] Jordan: ok next steps recap, priya - what are you taking away?
[08:03] Priya: deliverables: 1) share harness repo + example config (link will be sent) 2) intake customer's sample bundle and run smoke test (we aim to complete in 48 hours after receiving) 3) run ramp/peak tests and deliver CSV + dashboard 4) security checklist and network/IP ranges.
[08:23] Priya: estimated timeline: smoke within 2 days of intake, full benchmark within 1 week, results review within 9 business days.
[08:33] Evan: sounds good. one ask - can you surface cost tradeoffs for streaming vs non-streaming per-conversation? that's a key decision for product
[08:41] Priya: yes we'll include cost-per-conversation and cost-per-1k-requests in the final report and show token deltas and any re-send overheads
[08:51] Jordan: ok i'll send pricing ranges and can include estimated committed capacity numbers if you want a dedicated test pool pricing for comparison
[08:58] Rina: please also include audit log retention options and sample log snippets so compliance can review quickly
[09:05] Jordan: will do, we'll attach the SOC2 packet and an example audit log.
[09:12] Tom: last q - do you capture connection-level metrics for streaming (chunk RTT, reconnects)?
[09:18] Priya: yes we capture chunk RTT, chunk size distribution, reconnects per-session; we'll flag any abnormalities and include trace IDs for debugging.
[09:27] Evan: thanks all, we'll upload scripts to S3 and send a note in the CRM with link and access perms
[09:33] Jordan: great - thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the repo link and 48-hour smoke run plan.
[09:40] Meeting end
